OP-17 “The World's Strongest Warriors”: official release facts and sealed box research

Research and data: OP Box Index · Published July 17, 2026 · Updated August 10, 2026 · Data sources & methodology

This page separates published product facts from pre-release market observations. Bandai's English product page confirms the August 28 release, August 21 pre-release, USD $4.99 pack price, and 131+4 card types. Shueisha's official Shonen Jump card page lists the Japanese release on August 22 at ¥240 per six-card pack. OP Box Index does not publish a sealed-box market price until completed-sale data exists.

What the official pages establish

Bandai identifies OP-17 as the fourth-anniversary main booster and shows the English product's release schedule, price, total card-type count, and rarity families. The official page also presents Elbaf, the Rocks Pirates, and the Four Emperors as product themes. Those are product facts; they do not establish a secondary-market value.

The Japanese and English editions are separate products. The ¥240 Japanese pack figure must not be compared directly with a USD $4.99 English pack without accounting for pack contents, language, taxes, shipping, and local distribution. A retailer's display-box asking price is also not the same thing as Bandai's per-pack suggested price.

OP-17 box price, reprint status and factory-seal checks

Before release, most visible box prices are retailer or marketplace asks. They are not completed sales, and cancelled orders, deposits, allocation uncertainty, or mixed Japanese and English listings can distort them. For that reason, this page does not turn pre-order asks into a market median or a buy recommendation.

No source-backed OP-17 reprint can exist before the product's first Japanese release. Later restocks will be recorded only when a dated retailer or distributor source is available; pre-order inventory and rumours will not be relabelled as reprints.

For the Japanese display, the factory-seal standard is the original Bandai security tape in uncut condition. Added shrink does not replace that tape. The older launch pages for OP-14, OP-15, and OP-16 provide historical context, but their price paths do not predict OP-17. Once OP-17 has a valid sold sample, its own observation count, range, language, and date will appear here.

Confirmed card treatments, without price projections

Bandai's product presentation confirms a Super Leader Alt-Art treatment and identifies OP17-079 Monkey.D.Luffy as the shown example. It also presents Super Alt-Art cards, Treasure Rare, Special Cards, and anniversary-themed treatments. These details help identify the product, but no raw-card or PSA 10 value is assigned before matched sales exist.

Card reveals can change which listings attract attention, but attention is not a measured sale. Individual card pages are added only after the artwork, card number, language, condition, and sale record can be matched.

How to verify a sealed display

For a Japanese One Piece display, the primary factory-seal check is the original Bandai security tape in uncut condition. Added shrink is not a substitute for that tape. Photos should show the top tape, both side seams, bottom, product code, and any dents or tears. English displays use their region's factory wrapping and labeling, so the two seal standards should not be mixed.

A marketplace listing should also state the language and quantity clearly. Loose packs, opened displays, mixed-language lots, and listings that hide the seal area are excluded from OP Box Index's sealed-box comparisons.

When this page changes

After the Japanese and English releases, the page will add verified sold-price summaries only when the sample meets the rules in our methodology. Chase-card tables require matched printings, and grading figures remain population reports rather than estimates of how many sealed boxes were opened. Every material update receives a new visible review date.

Frequently asked questions

When does OP-17 release?

Shueisha's official card page lists August 22, 2026 for Japan. Bandai lists an August 21 English pre-release and August 28 English release.

What is the official OP-17 pack price?

The cited Japanese page lists ¥240 for a six-card pack. Bandai's English page lists USD $4.99 per pack. These are region-specific pack figures, not a secondary-market box quote.

What is an OP-17 sealed box worth before release?

No post-release sold sample exists yet. Pre-order asking prices are recorded separately and are not presented as established market value.

What seal should a Japanese OP-17 display have?

The original Bandai security tape should be present and uncut. Added shrink does not replace that factory-seal evidence.

Why is there no buy rating yet?

A rating before release would rely on asking prices and assumptions rather than completed-sale evidence. This page waits for a dated, language-matched sample.
